summary: This work systematically investigates TiN CPW resonators on 200 mm high-resistivity Si wafers, isolating how deposition conditions, dry-etch power, and resist-strip temperature affect two-level-system (TLS) losses across three distinct crystal orientations (111, 200, mixed). The dominant loss mechanism is interfacial oxide formation at metal-air and substrate-air interfaces during structuring, recoverable by buffered oxide etch, yielding $\delta_{\mathrm{TLS}} = 9.67 \times 10^{-7}$ and $Q_i \approx 10^6$.
motivation: Process-induced TLS losses at superconducting film interfaces limit qubit coherence and resonator quality factors; understanding which fabrication steps control these losses is essential for scaling TiN qubits to industry CMOS workflows.
method: Three TiN depositions with different crystal textures (controlled by sputtering parameters: temperature, power, gas ratios) were patterned using high-power (500 W, 180 V bias, overetch 20–100 nm) and low-power (70 W, 17 V bias, no overetch) dry etches, followed by hydrogen-plasma resist strips at 150 °C (LT) or 250 °C (HT). Resonators were characterized by XRD, four-point-probe sheet resistance, SEM, ellipsometry, RRR measurements, and cryogenic $S_{21}$ fitting to extract $\delta_{\mathrm{TLS}} = \delta_{\mathrm{LP}} - \delta_{\mathrm{HP}}$; participation-ratio modeling isolated loss contributions by interface.
result: Structuring dominates over material: low-power etch plus low-temperature strip minimizes losses ($\delta_{\mathrm{TLS}} \sim 10^{-6}$); high-temperature plasma grows lossy oxides (up to 3.2 nm) at grain boundaries; buffered oxide etch removes interfacial oxides and converges all prior process variants to $\delta_{\mathrm{TLS}} = 9.67 \times 10^{-7}$ and $\delta_{\mathrm{LP}} = 11.04 \times 10^{-7}$, with internal $Q_i$ approaching $10^6$.
